chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from 'Imran ibn Musa from Musa ibn Ja'far from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl from Ibn Bukayr from 'Abd al-A'la, the freedman of the House of Sam, regarding

the man who intends to travel in the month of Ramadan, he said: He breaks the fast, even if he departs a little before the sun sets. The ruling in this is what we have previously stated: that whoever departs after the sun has passed its zenith (dhuhr) and had spent the night with the intention of travel, it is permissible for him to break the fast, although it is preferable for him to fast until nightfall, according to what has preceded from the earlier narrations, and there is no contradiction between them.

key_terms.بَيَّتَ بِالنِّيَّة: spent the night with the intention

ai.seo_question: Can a traveler in Ramadan break their fast if they depart after dawn with the intention of travel?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfabar resolves the juristic debate regarding travelers who depart after dawn without prior intention, affirming the permissibility of breaking the fast while maintaining the superiority of continuing until sunset. It harmonizes with earlier traditions by distinguishing between the legal validity (jawaaz) and the recommended excellence (afdaliyya) of fasting, reflecting the Shia principle of reconciling seemingly divergent reports. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding travel conditions, prioritizing ease for the traveler while preserving the sanctity of the fast.
